note: Real-ELF ProgramTest for the RelayedMainnetStateV1 family in the Resolution role program: the observation-record transport (create/append/seal/retire), one consumption of a sealed record into a terminal certificate, and the funded liveness walk of MAINNET_STATE_RELAY.md section 4.8. Real compiled Core and Resolution ELFs; the Ed25519 signatures are cryptographically real and are verified by the runtime's own precompile before the program runs, but everything they attest is synthetic -- the account bytes are fixtures, the mainnet slot is a number, and the relayer key is generated in the test. This is NOT devnet evidence, NOT mainnet evidence, and NOT provider-availability evidence: the honest sentence about the strongest row here is 'the bank accepted an attestation asserting mainnet state', never 'the market observed mainnet'. Only the transactions bound below are recorded; the campaign's hostile corpora deliberately are not, because a campaign that labelled every transaction it happens to send would be claiming coverage no binding was written for. Wired 2026-08-27 (RES-FINISH) with the funded walk that made the family's terminal path reachable at all.

bindings.label: relayed transport: create the observation record
bindings.note: One RelayedObservationRecordV1 created at its derived address under the Resolution role, bound to the Market, generation, pinned account-set identity and observed slot. The record's Source graph coordinates ride the creation instruction because creation is the only route that has to be told them; every later route reads them back out of the persisted record.

bindings.label: relayed transport: append observation *
bindings.note: Four appends, one per pinned account-set position, each behind a real Ed25519 precompile instruction the runtime verifies before the program runs. The adapter folds each observation into the record's running set digest at the position the account set fixes, so the relayer chooses neither the order nor the membership.

bindings.label: relayed transport: seal the completed set
bindings.note: One key-set member's seal over the completed set, at a 1-of-1 threshold, moving the record Collecting -> Sealed. The seal covers the set digest the appends built, not the bytes the sealer supplies.

bindings.label: relayed transport: retire the record into the Market beneficiary
bindings.note: The record is closed and its rent returned to the Market's own persisted RentCredit beneficiary -- an account the adapter never derives, because Core already persists which account receives this Market's returned rent and the adapter can only agree with it.

bindings.label: relayed consumption: a sealed graduation resolves the market
bindings.note: One sealed record interpreted, under the CHAIN_STATE_SOURCES decoding rules, into a terminal SourceResolutionStateV2 and a ResolutionSuccess ResolutionCertificateV2. The Product -- not the venue table -- decides which outcome the decoded MigrationProgress discriminant selects. NOTE: this transaction serialises to 1,534 bytes, over Solana's 1,232-byte legacy packet maximum; see the packet witnesses.

bindings.label: relayed liveness: a silent market walks to its pre-disclosed failure
bindings.note: Section 4.8's headline property, executed: a market no relayer answered for walked Primary -> Exhausted -> FailureCommitted in one transition, minting a terminal ResolutionFailure certificate at the Product's own failure selector and crediting the walker the capability manifest's own quoted bounty out of the explicit-failure compartment the market escrowed at founding. Nothing in the frame is relayer-supplied: no record, no provider release, no adapter configuration, no key set, no venue.

bindings.label: relayed liveness: a walk before the deadline refuses
bindings.note: HOSTILE. Bounded in the direction that matters: the walk is a liveness path, not a way to end a market early. exhaust_after_primary_deadline refuses strictly before window.end + window.max_age, both of them the market's own founding-time content. Refuses Transition (0x800C); the campaign asserts the Source phase, both escrows, the walker's balance and both certificate addresses are unchanged.

bindings.label: relayed liveness: a second walk cannot collect the bounty twice
bindings.note: HOSTILE, and the one that would cost real money if it were wrong. After a committed walk the Source is terminal and the certificate PDA is occupied, so the second attempt has several independent reasons to refuse -- and the one it REACHES is Funding (14), not Transition (12), because plan_deadline_failure_v1 debits before it transitions and the compartment's bounty is already spent. A walk that cannot be paid for cannot move the market. The campaign asserts the escrow pays nobody a second time.

bindings.label: relayed liveness: a live compartment that is not the escrow refuses
bindings.note: HOSTILE, substituted compensation. The exhaustion compartment is a REAL FundingStateV1 of this same market, Active, owned by the Resolution program, at its own correctly derived address -- every check about shape passes on it. What refuses is the check about identity: the explicit-failure compartment is the one whose manifest entry configures this market's own Source material, exactly the binding core_effect's authenticate_funding_entries established when the three compartments were created. Refuses Funding (0x800E) by that comparison rather than by an account-position convention, which is what makes the refusal survive a frame reordering.

bindings.label: relayed liveness: an escrow one lamport short refuses
bindings.note: HOSTILE, unfunded shape. The FundingStateV1 bytes stay exactly canonical -- same entry index, same manifest, same Active status, same derived address -- and one lamport goes missing from the account. That is the only way to reach validate_against's custody comparison at all, because the address folds in the state's own bytes. Refuses Funding (0x800E). Without the check a route could pay a bounty out of an account it was about to leave below its own Rent reserve, and the shortfall would surface an instruction later as an unrelated rent failure.
